episodes.202424: A slow-moving warm front in an extremely moist (PWAT values exceeding 2.00, values closer to 2.25 across the Lower Susquehanna Valley) and unstable environment allowed for multiple clusters of thunderstorms to begin to form during the late morning hours and continue through the late evening hours of June 30, 2025. A shortwave trough stationed across the region allowed for enhanced lift, with relatively weak shear in place, bringing a severe threat in the form of wet downbursts and a flash flood threat given training thunderstorms with efficient rainfall rates in excess of two inches per hour across southern Pennsylvania. Isolated thunderstorm wind damage was observed across Tioga County, with tree damage observed in Lancaster County and a widespread area of trees and wires knocked down in Cumberland County due to a wet microburst. Multiple rounds of thunderstorms during the afternoon and evening hours across Lancaster County, where multiple days of heavy rainfall led to low flash flood guidance, prompted widespread flash flooding across the northern half of the county, with multiple water rescues reported in Mount Joy and Manheim. Multiple roadways were closed across northern Lancaster County and southern Lebanon County due to heavy rain, with isolated instances of flash flooding in Cumberland County. Flooding concerns in Lancaster County continued into the early morning hours of July 1, 2025 as the heaviest rain began to move out of the area.
episodes.202445: Amidst afternoon thunderstorm activity, outflow gusts surging through the Tijeras Canyon produced severe wind gusts that blew up abundant amounts of dust in the southern Albuquerque metro area. This dust produced an area of low visibility.
episodes.202481: Numerous thunderstorms erupted over southern WI ahead of a slow moving cold front. Damaging downburst winds occurred in and around Timmerman Field in Milwaukee. Urban and small stream flooding occurred in Pardeeville and Janesville.
episodes.202499: A boundary stalled across northeast Maryland and interacted with the Chesapeake Bay breeze to result in a nearly stationary thunderstorm across Baltimore and Harford counties for much of the late afternoon and evening. Localized rainfall amounts of two to six inches were observed, with instances of flash flooding.
episodes.202665: Strong/severe thunderstorms formed over the foothills of Larimer County during the afternoon of June 29th, producing large hail. Only 1 inch diameter hail reports were received with these storms, but radar support golf ball or larger for brief moments. Storms weakened as the pushed eastward. Eventually another severe thunderstorm formed during the early evening hours.
episodes.202694: Thunderstorms occurred during the early morning hours across central Missouri, producing localized flash flooding. A larger complex of thunderstorms with severe winds moved through southwest Missouri during the afternoon and evening hours of June 29th, producing widespread damaging winds from Dade County, southeast into the Springfield metro area and then southeast into Taney County. Widespread power outages and damage to electrical infrastructure occurred across the Springfield metro area with over 50,000 customers without power across Springfield-Greene County. There was one fatality and five injuries due to the thunderstorms. ||Additionally, flash flooding also occurred behind this area of thunderstorms across southern Missouri. Total rainfall amounts of 3-6 inches occurred across central Missouri from Morgan County southeast to Dent and Shannon Counties.
episodes.202700: A period of heavy rain across northeast South Dakota resulted in downstream river gauges within the upper and middle Big Sioux River Basin to rise into Minor and locally Moderate flood stage.
episodes.202710: A slow-moving cold front interacted with a hot and humid airmass that was in place across central Illinois, resulting in clusters of strong thunderstorms developing during the afternoon of June 30th, 2025. Most of these storms were below severe limits, but one produced isolated wind damage in southwestern McLean County.
episodes.202750: Scattered severe thunderstorms developed on the western periphery of thunderstorm outflow, associated with an intense complex of thunderstorms across the Ozarks, on the evening of the 29th. This activity eventually moved from south-central Kansas into northern Oklahoma late in the evening, producing a few reports/observations of severe winds, mainly along additional thunderstorm outflow(s).
episodes.202751: Widespread strong-to-severe thunderstorms developed along a quasi-stationary boundary across central and southern Oklahoma and western-north Texas during the evening of the 30th. In addition to a measured severe-caliber wind gust, the combination of high moisture content in the lower atmosphere and slow-moving thunderstorms led to a few localized areas of flash flooding across southern Oklahoma.
episodes.203165: Numerous thunderstorms developed across southeast Wyoming during the afternoon of June 29th. These thunderstorms moved eastward and produce some very large hail and damaging winds as they turned severe.
episodes.203166: Numerous thunderstorms developed across eastern Wyoming during the afternoon of June 29th. These thunderstorms moved eastward into western Nebraska and produce some very large hail and damaging winds.
episodes.203235: A couple rounds of scattered heavy rains from late on the 28th through the morning of the 29th brought 1 to 2 inches of rainfall, to several areas from Bloomington into parts of Brown County and Lawrence County.  Soon after, more impressive rainfall rates occurred over the same areas from the 29th evening into very early on the 30th, where an additional 3 to 6 inches of rainfall fell on a few local areas.||Resultant totals of 3 to 7 inches over a broad area from Bloomington and Nashville, southwest to northern portions of both Daviess County and Lawrence County, produced scattered flooding.  Flash flooding occurred in several embedded areas, with water flowing over roads.  Most notable was water up to a foot deep on the south side of Bloomington.
episodes.203316: A few severe thunderstorms affected eastern West Virginia and northern Maryland with localized damaging downbursts.
episodes.203317: A few severe thunderstorms affected eastern West Virginia and northern Maryland with localized damaging downbursts.
episodes.203503: Scattered thunderstorms moved through the region in association with an upper level disturbance.
episodes.203515: Scattered thunderstorms developed in a warm and humid airmass.
episodes.203547: Severe thunderstorms, over southwestern South Dakota and the northwestern Nebraska Panhandle, tracked to the southeast, crossing the western Sandhills and southwestern Nebraska during the evening hours of June 29th. This activity persisted into the late evening hours, before exiting portions of southwestern and central Nebraska during the early overnight hours of June 30th. Hail up to 2 inches in diameter and thunderstorm wind gusts up to 64 MPH were reported with the most intense storms.
episodes.203660: Thunderstorms developed across northeastern Oklahoma and southeastern Kansas during the evening of the 29th, along an outflow boundary that settled across the region from thunderstorms to the east. The strongest thunderstorms produced large hail up to golf ball size and damaging wind as they moved southeastward across the area.
episodes.203727: A mid level disturbance over the eastern gulf and light surface flow produces widely scattered convection over the eastern gulf leading to gusty marine winds over Cedar Key area waters.
episodes.203807: A slow-moving cold front ahead of an approaching shortwave trough resulted in numerous thunderstorms across the Permian Basin. Flash flooding and damaging winds were reported in some locations.
episodes.203918: Southwest flow over a moist and diurnally unstable airmass triggered isolated strong to severe storms along sea breeze and boundary mergers toward the I-95 corridor in the mid-afternoon. Storm mergers produced very heavy rainfall rates where localized flash flooding occurred.
episodes.203919: Southwest flow over a moist and diurnally unstable airmass with slow storm motion produced flash flooding where boundaries merged along sea breezes and outflows in the afternoon across the Jacksonville downtown area.
episodes.203920: A cluster of thunderstorms developed across eastern Colorado and resulted in wind gusts ranging from 58-61 mph across Cheyenne county, with the strongest occurring near Cheyenne Wells.
episodes.203944: In the overnight hours of the 29th, storms formed in Colorado and Nebraska before pushing into northwestern Kansas. Around midnight, numerous clusters of storms formed and intensified across northwestern Kansas and progressed to the southeast. These storms produced 60 MPH winds and hail up to 1.25 inches.
episodes.204058: A cold front moved into a warm and unstable airmass, producing strong to severe thunderstorms and damaging wind gusts. A storm along the sea-breeze also produced a brief tornado.
episodes.204059: A cold front moved into a warm and unstable airmass, producing strong to severe thunderstorms and damaging wind gusts across portions of New Jersey.
episodes.204060: A cold front moved into a warm and unstable airmass, producing strong to severe thunderstorms and damaging wind gusts across portions of eastern Pennsylvania.
episodes.204107: Scattered storms developed on the afternoon of June 30 over northern Minnesota and Wisconsin, traveling southeast through the evening. One storm produced hail up to quarter size in St Croix County and another knocked down several trees within the town of Cornell in Chippewa County.
episodes.204118: Scattered thunderstorms, out ahead of a cold front, produced heavy rain across portions of the Delaware Valley.
episodes.204205: Dry air at the surface with some mid-level moisture and a weak upper trough combined to create thunderstorms with gusty outflow winds which also resulted in a dust storm over the Lordsburg Playa.
episodes.204274: Weather pattern setup across western SD that allowed for storms to develop and produce large hail and heavy rainfall across the area.
episodes.204396: Warm temperatures on the afternoon of the 29th allowed scattered thunderstorms to develop across the South Plains. Although no reports of severe weather were received, nickel size hail was reported in the town of Farwell (Parmer County).
episodes.204410: After a break in Monsoon activity, thunderstorms came off the White Mountains causing severe winds in Safford, AZ and sent an outflow sending a dust storm to the Tucson Metro area and Cochise County.
episodes.204599: Strong thunderstorms produced several observed wind gusts in excess of 50 mph.  A peak wind gust of 68 mph was measured by the South Dakota Department of Transportation mesonet station 4 miles west northwest of Cresbard. Winds would be strong enough to damage several small trees on the south side of the city of Aberdeen.
episodes.204640: A series of largely sub-severe thunderstorms moved across northeastern and east-central Illinois during the afternoon and evening of the 29th. A few storms were stronger than the rest producing damaging winds and heavy rainfall, namely in Ford and Lake Counties.
episodes.204750: River flooding was observed at a couple points along the Black River.
episodes.204852: A cold front passed through Upper Michigan on the 30th, causing tree damage to the central and eastern portions of the region.
episodes.204910: On the afternoon of Monday June 30th, strong thunderstorms developed along a warm front tracking northeast across Lake Erie and the western New York area. One of these thunderstorms developed a waterspout over Lake Erie, offshore from Dunkirk, New York.
episodes.204931: Summertime convection developed in a regime of high moisture throughout the atmospheric column as well as high instability. One storm was able to reach severe limits and produced a downburst.
episodes.204932: Summertime convection developed in a regime of high moisture throughout the atmospheric column as well as high instability. One storm was able to reach severe limits and produced a downburst.
episodes.205155: Scattered severe storms moved across central, south central and southeast Kansas during the evening of the 29th into the early morning hours of the 30th. These storms produced up to ping pong ball sized hail and 72 mph winds.
